target_customer: Row crop growers and seed or trait companies that need durable disease and pest resistance, starting with soybean growers hit by soybean cyst nematode
problem: Pests and pathogens cause very large crop losses, agrochemicals are losing effectiveness, and natural resistance genes are overcome as pathogens evolve.
business_model: Trait development and licensing of engineered resistance genes (pre-revenue R&D, no pricing public)
product_category: Agricultural biotech, protein-engineered plant disease resistance traits

founders.name: PJ Steiner
education: MIT, SB and MEng in computer science
University of Cambridge, PhD in synthetic biology
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: postdoc at UC San Diego, two years as a scientist at Bolt Threads, then CU Boulder on a DARPA plant biosensor project.

founders.name: Matthew Bedewitz
education: Michigan State University, BS horticulture science
Michigan State University, PhD plant breeding, genetics and biotechnology
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: plant biochemist, postdoc at CU Boulder, met Steiner on the DARPA protein engineering project.

competitors.name: Resurrect Bio
competitors.what: UK startup engineering plant immune systems for disease resistance in crops

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing protein-based resistance genes that block pathogen effectors and proving them in crops needs protein engineering, plant transformation and field validation, which is research-grade for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Patentable engineered proteins and long trial cycles protect traits, but the company must license through large seed firms and no traction is public.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents run their own trait programs and partner with startups such as Tropic; no public action against Ohmic found.

market_need_then: The company cites hundreds of billions of dollars in annual losses to pests and pathogens, and its first target, soybean cyst nematode, is said by the company to cost over 1.5B USD a year in US yield; agrochemicals were described as no longer working.

branding.domain_note: Uses ohmicbiosciences.com, a descriptive suffix domain; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Not described in any source found
identity.visual_style: Minimal one page site with tagline and social links

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand was found; the site is a bare tagline page.

outcome_analysis: Ohmic is still active as of the latest sources, with two PhD founders who met on a DARPA plant biosensor project. Its only recorded funding is a small pre-seed tied to YC, so it remains early, with long trait development timelines and no public sign of an exit, layoffs or a larger round.
notes: Pre-seed of about 500K USD and its date (September or October 2023) come from aggregators VCBacked and Persana; PitchBook lists Y Combinator and Climate Capital as investors. No SEC Form D found. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoff news. Founding year 2021 per YC page. Tropic Biosciences was seen only in undated sources and is omitted from competitors.
